recipes.name: Seafood Paella inspired by Parks and Rec
ingredients: 1 tbsp kosher salt, divided + more to taste
1 3/4 lbs head on prawns (or large shrimp)
8 oz cuttlefish or squid, cleaned + diced
64 oz Fortified Fish Stock (see recipe below), divided
instructions: For the Shrimp Brine
Combine the salt and baking soda in a small bowl. Whisk to combine, then reserve until ready to use. - 1 tsp kosher salt - ¼ tsp baking soda
For the Seafood Paella
Add salt to a large bowl of water. Add the clam and allow them to soak for at least 1 hour, this will help remove grit from the clams. - 1 tbsp kosher salt divided + more to taste - 8 oz fresh clams

Remove the heads, peel, and devein (if necessary) all but 4-6 of the prawns, these will be reserved for presentation. Reserve the heads and shells for the Fortified Fish Stock (see recipe below). - 1 ¾ lbs head on prawns (or large shrimp)

Combine the Shrimp Brine and peeled prawns in a medium bowl. Using gloved hands, massage the brine into the shrimp. Reserve the prawns at room temperature for 30 minutes before cooking. - Shrimp Brine (see recipe above)
Heat the olive oil in a large paella pan over medium heat. Season the oil with 1 teaspoon of salt. - ¼ cup olive oil

Add the head-on prawns to the oil and cook on each side for 30 - 45 seconds, or until the shells turn right orange. Then, remove the prawns from the pan and reserve. This will only par-cook the prawns.

Add the onion and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the onion turns translucent. Add the garlic and stir the vegetables with a metal slotted spoon or wooden spatula. Cook the mixture for 30 seconds or until the garlic is fragrant. - 1 yellow onion finely chopped - 4 cloves garlic minced
Add the cuttlefish/squid to the pan and stir to combine the ingredients. Cook for 1-2 minutes or until the cuttlefish turns opaque. - 8 oz cuttlefish or squid cleaned + diced
Create a well in the center of the paella pan, then add the sweet paprika. Toast the paprika for 15 seconds, then stir to combine the ingredients. - 2 ½ tsp Spanish sweet smoked paprika (pimenton)
Add the grated tomato mixture to the pan and stir to combine. Cook the mixture until most of the water has evaporated, about 2-4 minutes. - 2 ½ large ripe tomatoes grated
Add the paella rice and stir to combine once more. Toast the rice for 1 minute. - 1 lb Spanish paella rice

Combine 1/8th of the Fortified Fish Stock and the saffron in a small bowl. Stir the mixture until the stock is tinted by the saffron, then add it to the paella pan. - 8 oz Fortified Fish Stock (see recipe below) divided - 1 tsp saffron threads

Then add the remaining Fortified Fish Stock and the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt to the pan. Stir to evenly distribute the rice. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat and cook for the rice for 10 minutes. - 56 oz Fortified Fish Stock (see recipe below) divided - 1 tbsp kosher salt divided + more to taste

After about 10 minutes, about 75 percent of the water should be evaporated. At this point, nestle the clams and mussels into the rice and remaining cooking liquid. Arrange the uncooked prawns around the pan and lay the seared head-on prawns in a decorative pattern on top of the paella. - 8 oz fresh clams - 8 oz fresh mussels cleaned - 1 ¾ lbs head on prawns (or large shrimp)

Turn the heat to low and continue cooking the paella for 5-10 minutes longer, or until almost all of the moisture has evaporated, the rice is al dente, and the prawns, clams, and mussels have all cooked through. The bottom of the the paella should be lightly caramelized/toasted, this is called socarrat and it is the sign of a well prepared paella!
Turn the heat off entirely and cover the paella with a large clean dish towel. Allow the paella to rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with lemon wedges and serve! - To garnish: lemon wedges
For the Fortified Fish Stock
Heat the oil in a large stock pot over medium heat. - 1 tbsp olive oil

Once the oil is preheated, add the prawn shells and cook for 1-2 minutes or until well toasted. Then add the onion and garlic cloves, toss to coat the ingredients in the oil and continue to cook the mixture for 1 minute longer. - 1 lb prawn heads/shells - 1 onion quartered - 2 cloves garlic

Add enough fish stock (or water), parsley stems, peppercorns, and bay leaves. Then, bring the mixture to a simmer. Skim off any scum that comes to the surface. - 64 oz fish stock (or water) - 4 ½ parsley stems - 2 tsp black peppercorns - 2 bay leaves
Continue simmering the stock for 30 minutes over medium low heat.
Strain and reserve the stock until ready to use. Alternatively, chill the stock over an ice bath until it reaches 70 °F. Then refrigerate the stock for up to 1 week or freeze for up to 3 months.
